nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: How have carbon price prediction approaches evolved in recent years?
nodes.answer: Various carbon price prediction approaches have emerged, which can be broadly classified into three categories: traditional econometric methods, artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, and hybrid models.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Carbon offset programs|Innovation in carbon offset methodologies_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How do hybrid models improve prediction outcomes in carbon price forecasting?
nodes.answer: Hybrid models improve prediction outcomes by integrating the abilities of each algorithm, diversifying the risk of single methods, and exploring complex internal information from various angles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Carbon offset programs|Innovation in carbon offset methodologies_qna_002
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: Which decomposition technique has been widely employed for maximizing forecasting precision in carbon prices?
nodes.answer: Empirical mode decomposition (EMD) has been widely employed for maximizing forecasting precision in carbon prices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Carbon offset programs|Innovation in carbon offset methodologies_qna_003
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What method has been introduced to improve prediction results in carbon price forecasting?
nodes.answer: A reconstruction method has been introduced, using sample entropy (SE) to reconstitute subgroups into new components, which helps avoid errors of subjective selection.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Carbon offset programs|Innovation in carbon offset methodologies_qna_004
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What technique is commonly used in literature to predict carbon prices?
nodes.answer: A two-step technique involving decomposition followed by a single learning method is widely used to improve prediction accuracy.
